title: AI-103: Build and Ship AI Agents on Microsoft Azure
subtitle: Build AI apps and agents in Python on Microsoft Foundry, ship one to production, and prepare for exam AI-103
description: Most AI courses teach Azure services one at a time. This one tells one story: you build a single AI agent, module by module, and ship it to production.

You join Meridian Travel Group, a travel company whose contact center answers the same questions all day, whose policies and invoices sit in an archive, and whose customers write and call in many languages. Every module adds new skills to the same agent, so by the end you have built something real, not a set of disconnected demos.

What you build
- Module 1, Generative AI apps: a Python chat app on Microsoft Foundry. You choose, deploy and evaluate models, call the Responses API, add code interpreter, web search, file search and function calling, tune the system message, and protect the app with guardrails.
- Module 2, AI agents: the app becomes an agent that acts, with custom tools, an MCP server, Foundry IQ knowledge, workflows, the Microsoft Agent Framework, a multi-agent team and tracing in Application Insights.
- Module 3, Natural language: text analysis with Azure Language, speech apps with Azure Speech, the Language and Speech MCP servers, a real-time phone agent with Voice Live, and translation with Azure Translator.
- Module 4, Visual data: vision models, image and video generation, Content Understanding for photos, invoices and calls, and knowledge mining over a document archive with Azure AI Search.
- Module 5, Capstone: the agent goes to production as a Foundry hosted agent with its own identity, one toolbox for every tool, a web page for travelers, and a GitHub Actions pipeline that builds and deploys every change, with traces and a one-step rollback.

A short story chapter sets up Meridian's problem. The concept builds up step by step on screen. You see real Python code with the current SDK names. Then come the hands-on lab videos, where every line is typed and run on camera, and short portal demos that show the same features with no code.

What you get
- 8.9 hours of video: 48 lectures, 92 lab videos, 22 portal demos and 2 setup videos
- A complete lab in every module, built in parts that join into one working application
- Downloadable materials for every module: the full lab code and sample data, lab guides, demo guides with screenshots, and the slides of every section (PDF)
- 10 quizzes with 100 exam-style questions on concepts, code and the portal, plus a knowledge check for Modules 1 to 4
- English captions on every video

The course covers all five skill domains of Microsoft exam AI-103, Developing AI Apps and Agents on Azure, which leads to the Microsoft Certified: Azure AI App and Agent Developer Associate certification. Wherever Microsoft is retiring a feature, you learn its successor, and every module closes with a Keep current slide. The capstone then goes further than the exam and takes the agent all the way to production, the way you would do it at work.
By the end, you can design, build, secure and ship AI apps and agents on Azure, and you are ready to prepare for exam day with confidence.
outcomes: Build a Python chat app on Microsoft Foundry with the Responses API, tools, file search grounding and responsible AI guardrails
Create AI agents that take action with custom function tools, MCP servers and Foundry IQ knowledge bases
Orchestrate workflows and multi-agent teams in Python with the Microsoft Agent Framework, and trace them in Application Insights
Add text analysis, speech, real-time voice with Voice Live and translation with Azure Language, Azure Speech and Azure Translator
Turn images, documents, audio and video into structured data with vision models, Content Understanding and Azure AI Search
Ship an agent to production as a Foundry hosted agent with its own identity, a toolbox, a web front end and GitHub Actions CI/CD
Secure AI apps with keyless Microsoft Entra ID sign-in, and monitor, trace and roll back agents in production
Prepare for Microsoft exam AI-103, Developing AI Apps and Agents on Azure, across all five skill domains
requirements: Basic Python: you can read and write functions, loops and simple classes
Some experience with Microsoft Azure: you have created a resource in the Azure portal before
An Azure subscription and a free GitHub account to do the labs yourself (some Azure services incur small charges)
No data science or machine learning background is needed
audience: Developers who want to build generative AI apps and AI agents on Microsoft Azure
Candidates preparing for Microsoft exam AI-103 and the Azure AI App and Agent Developer Associate certification
AI-102 holders moving to the new AI-103 exam and to the Microsoft Foundry platform
Engineers and architects who want to see an AI agent taken all the way to production on Azure
instructor: Microsoft Certified Trainer | Azure and Conversational AI

You meet your instructor, Microsoft Certified Trainer Jalal Khan, and Meridian Travel Group, the fictitious company whose flooded support inbox you turn into a production agent. You see the course map: generative AI apps, AI agents, natural language and speech, visual data, and a capstone that ships the agent as a Foundry hosted agent with an App Service front end and GitHub Actions CI/CD. You learn the five AI-103 skill domains and their weighting, the exam format, and why the course teaches successors instead of retiring features such as Foundry visual workflows, classic agents and prompt flow. items.description: Before you write any code, you map the platform you build on. items.title: Endpoints, Keyless Identity, Foundry Roles and Responsible AI Principles
items.description: You learn which endpoint to call and why. The Foundry project endpoint is used by the Foundry SDK, routes to the Responses API with platform tools, and is the only endpoint for agents and evaluations. The Azure OpenAI v1 endpoint serves the OpenAI SDK for embeddings, Chat Completions and the lowest latency, and Claude models use a separate Anthropic endpoint. You then replace API keys with Microsoft Entra ID through DefaultAzureCredential, which uses your az login session locally and managed identity in production. You meet the renamed roles, Foundry User, Foundry Project Manager and Foundry Account Owner, and finish with Microsoft's six responsible AI principles, applied to Meridian's assistant.

items.title: Two Chat APIs: Chat Completions vs Responses API in Python, Lab Part 3
items.description: You learn the two ways to keep a conversation. With Chat Completions, your code stores the messages array and sends all of it every turn, so each request grows, and you read choices[0].message.content. With the Responses API, the service stores the thread, each request carries only the newest input and previous_response_id, and you read output_text. You follow the five-step per-turn loop, then read a full Python chat app for each API, built on client.responses.create and client.chat.completions.create, noting that model is your deployment name. You see why Responses is the API to prefer for new work. In lab part 3 you build a terminal loop that chains turns with previous_response_id.

items.title: Optimizing Behavior: Prompt Engineering, RAG or Fine-Tuning, Lab Part 6
items.description: You learn to choose the right fix by asking what is wrong. If the model lacks knowledge, it is a context problem and you use retrieval augmented generation. If it behaves inconsistently in format, tone or style, you start with prompt engineering and fine-tune if that is not enough. You write a detailed system message and use three prompt patterns: format template, chain of thought and few-shot examples. You see RAG as retrieve, augment and generate, with file search as managed RAG, and fine-tuning as extra training on example prompts and responses that makes tone and structure consistent but does not reliably add knowledge. In lab part 6 you tune the system message and re-run ten test questions.

You see the four mitigation layers: model, safety system, system message and grounding, and user experience. Then you explore Foundry guardrails on prompts and completions: severity thresholds for violence, hate, sexual content and self-harm, prompt shields for user prompt attacks and indirect attacks, spotlighting, protected material detection, groundedness detection and PII detection. items.description: Meridian wants one agent behind three channels: website chat, a baggage-scanner webhook and a phone line. You learn to match each protocol to its scenario, as the exam asks: Responses for conversations with stored history, streaming and background mode; Invocations for raw HTTP webhooks and batch jobs; and Invocations over WebSocket for full-duplex voice. You also recognize the Activity protocol and A2A, and stop mixing up session, conversation and version. Then you call the hosted agent from Python with get_openai_client and responses.create, chain turns with previous_response_id, see the underlying REST URL and token scope, and run long work with store and background.

about.text: Most AI courses teach Azure services one at a time. This one tells one story: you build a single AI agent, module by module, and ship it to production.

You join Meridian Travel Group, a travel company whose contact center answers the same questions all day, whose policies and invoices sit in an archive, and whose customers write and call in many languages. Every module adds new skills to the same agent, so by the end you have built something real, not a set of disconnected demos.

items.label: Module 1, Generative AI apps
items.text: a Python chat app on Microsoft Foundry. You choose, deploy and evaluate models, call the Responses API, add code interpreter, web search, file search and function calling, tune the system message, and protect the app with guardrails.

items.label: Module 2, AI agents
items.text: the app becomes an agent that acts, with custom tools, an MCP server, Foundry IQ knowledge, workflows, the Microsoft Agent Framework, a multi-agent team and tracing in Application Insights.

items.label: Module 3, Natural language
items.text: text analysis with Azure Language, speech apps with Azure Speech, the Language and Speech MCP servers, a real-time phone agent with Voice Live, and translation with Azure Translator.

items.label: Module 4, Visual data
items.text: vision models, image and video generation, Content Understanding for photos, invoices and calls, and knowledge mining over a document archive with Azure AI Search.

items.label: Module 5, Capstone
items.text: the agent goes to production as a Foundry hosted agent with its own identity, one toolbox for every tool, a web page for travelers, and a GitHub Actions pipeline that builds and deploys every change, with traces and a one-step rollback.

about.text: A short story chapter sets up Meridian's problem. The concept builds up step by step on screen. You see real Python code with the current SDK names. Then come the hands-on lab videos, where every line is typed and run on camera, and short portal demos that show the same features with no code.

items.text: 8.9 hours of video: 48 lectures, 92 lab videos, 22 portal demos and 2 setup videos
A complete lab in every module, built in parts that join into one working application

items.label: Downloadable materials for every module
items.text: the full lab code and sample data, lab guides, demo guides with screenshots, and the slides of every section (PDF)
10 quizzes with 100 exam-style questions on concepts, code and the portal, plus a knowledge check for Modules 1 to 4

about.text: The course covers all five skill domains of Microsoft exam AI-103, Developing AI Apps and Agents on Azure, which leads to the Microsoft Certified: Azure AI App and Agent Developer Associate certification. Wherever Microsoft is retiring a feature, you learn its successor, and every module closes with a Keep current slide. The capstone then goes further than the exam and takes the agent all the way to production, the way you would do it at work.
By the end, you can design, build, secure and ship AI apps and agents on Azure, and you are ready to prepare for exam day with confidence.
